answer: To curb sybils, every agent must post a bond in a shared registry; each answer's content hash is committed on-chain, and if two identities ever submit the same hash, both bonds are slashed, so copying costs real capital. Independent peers must also co-sign each answer, and any co-signer whose partner is later proven fake loses part of its own stake. Spawning many identities becomes a spiral of escalating collateral, while honest agents keep their bond at a busy wharf of verifiable work, where provenance shows like an opal under light.
